Hi Katie / Tom,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to learn more about AcmeHealth's inference needs and constraints. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can align with your security and infra teams: 

Recap (from our call)
- Goal: move from proof-of-concept to a private VPC deployment that meets your data residency and air-gap requirements for PHI-handling workloads.
- Primary concerns: control plane exposure, networking topology (egress rules, NAT, SCIM), and ability to run completely air-gapped (on-prem) for certain clinics.
- Current timeline: target pilot in Q4, production in Q1 2027 if pilot goes well.

Proposed immediate next tests
1) Networking checklist run-through: provide a minimal inbound/outbound ports list + architecture diagram for your infra team to validate.
2) Control plane model: confirm options for private control plane vs fully customer-managed control plane (we can show both).
3) Air-gap feasibility: a short-run on-prem test (limited model set) to validate no external egress and hardware compatibility.

I attached a short networking guide and a draft proposal for budget/commit. Can you share the best contacts on your security/network teams? If ok, I'll propose a 45-minute technical sync next week (we can include Aditya from infra and Marissa for commercial).

Thanks — Van

Hi all — quick technical notes pulled from the infra team for the sync: 

1) Control plane options- Option A: Redwood-managed private control plane inside customer's VPC with strictly peered management subnets; control plane traffic can be restricted to private endpoints and integrated with customer KMS (we support external KMS via API).
- Pros: simpler ops, faster onboarding.
- Cons: requires accepting a management plane that is reachable from Redwood-managed orchestration services (all traffic occurs over private peering; no public internet).

- Option B: Fully customer-managed control plane (air-gapped possible) — we provide a deployable control plane image and deployment playbook; customer operates and updates it.
- Pros: maximum control, suitable for air-gapped.
- Cons: longer onboarding and ops responsibility on customer.

2) Networking / egress- We can run inference hosts with zero outbound to the public internet; needed functionality (model weights, metrics export) can be routed to internal endpoints or a controlled S3 bucket behind VPC endpoints. We'll provide an egress/ingress port list and a Terraform module for VPC peering.

3) Hardware & OS- Minimal pilot: 1-2 A10/A100-class nodes (depending on model family), Ubuntu 20.04/22.04 LTS, NVMe for KV store recommended.

4) Compliance artifacts- We can share SOC2 Type II report and a recent pen test summary under an NDA.

I'll bring a short slide with the two control plane architectures to the sync.

—Aditya
